content:
We've now been using iOS 27 for two months. It's still in beta, of course—about four to six weeks out from its official launch. That said, even though I've been running the beta on my phone for the past two months, I barely notice it's there. It just... works.

I still, of course, scramble to install the latest beta every few weeks in the Software Update screen. That's the only part of the beta experience that's remained consistent cycle 27.

Beyond that, I can't think of the usual things you'd say about a beta. Battery drain is essentially nonexistent, the phone doesn't run hot, and there isn't a pile of weird bugs or random SpringBoard resprings.

iOS 27 lets you enjoy all the benefits of new software—Siri AI, AirPods EQ, the new Wallet passes in Safari, beefier photo AI editing, and more—without any of the issues that typically come with running the bleeding-edge beta. Honestly, it's a bit surprising.

It might also be because iOS 26 was unstable out of the gate. Especially iOS 26.5, which for some reason (at least for me) caused constant resprings.

Of course, this is all anecdotal, but ask just about anyone and you'll hear them tell a similar tale of iOS 26 not being so great for them, either.

iOS 27 is genuinely excellent

Overall, iOS 27 delivers in terms of speed improvements, bug fixes, stability, and quality-of-life improvements. You might not notice it immediately because Siri AI is doing a lot of background indexing—but Apple already shipped iOS 26.6, so by the time you upgrade to iOS 27, it's already begun indexing for Siri AI in the background, and you don't have to do anything. Smooth sailing from there.

Most Liked Comment by Uno

While I largely agree that the iOS 27 (and WatchOS 27) betas have been noticeably more stable and battery-friendly than previous iOS betas, I have to push back on Siri. In the two iOS/WatchOS 27 betas released so far, Siri has basically been completely useless. Typing into the Siri app works fine, but using voice commands has been incredibly frustrating and a complete waste of time.

This is, of course, purely based on my personal experience.

I'm very much looking forward to iOS 27 rolling out to the public next month. It's a bit hard to believe, but Apple seems to have actually addressed most of the major pain points in iOS. Software will never be perfect, of course—but this is absolutely the smoothest my iPhone has been in recent memory.

iOS 27 will support every iPhone model that supported iOS 26, going all the way back to the iPhone 11 and later.
